notes.text: Trevor van Riemsdyk has not dressed for the last 15 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Declan Carlile has taken his spot beside Kris Letang. That pair has had 56% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 97:16 together, up from 39% with van Riemsdyk.

Elmer Söderblom is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Rutger McGroarty has taken his spot beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve and has missed the last 10 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 58% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 66:42 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Trevor van Riemsdyk is expected back after missing 15 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
Nick Robertson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 30% of the team’s shorthanded time in 20 games, up from 2% with his old team last season.

story.head: Iron sharpens iron
paras: The Blues (10-9-2) beat Anaheim 8-6 on Tuesday, while the Penguins (7-11-2) lost 4-1 to Ottawa on Saturday. Going in, the Blues are seventh in the Central (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Pens seventh in the Metropolitan (28th).

The Blues have played better than their record (.524) says: their chances are worth about .579, and their finishing has held them back. So have the Penguins (.400 on chances worth .543), where their finishing has held them back.

The Blues ice the puck less than anyone (1st), keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd). The Penguins get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). They also sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), so the Blues have the edge over them on forecheck pressure. The Penguins’ good looks will be harder to come by against the Blues.

Robert Thomas (4 G / 13 A / 17 P in 21 GP) leads the Blues in scoring, with a point in five straight games against Pittsburgh. Jimmy Snuggerud (10 G / 5 A / 15 P in 21 GP) has a team-high ten goals. For the Penguins, Erik Karlsson (3 G / 16 A / 19 P in 20 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Tommy Novak (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 20 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
Joel Hofer (8-6-1 / .922 SV% in 15 GS) has been terrific for St. Louis and is expected to start. Artūrs Šilovs (5-6-1 / .873 SV% in 12 GS) is expected to go for Pittsburgh.

Robert Thomas is one assist from passing Alex Pietrangelo for third on the Blues’ all-time assists list.
